new.n: The receiver's lost gold: a Port Sheldon capitalist's buried money (1830s)
new.pl: Port Sheldon townsite at Pigeon Lake, Ottawa Co (GNIS Port Sheldon); Ottawa House site once marked by its avenue of maples
new.st: When the 1830s Port Sheldon land-company city failed, 'one of the capitalists buried what money he had' to keep it from the receivers. 'The shifting sands covered the spot', and though he 'searched for many a day' the money eluded him. In 1921 the Ottawa House hotel site was still marked by the decayed maples of its avenue; its lumber went into a barn E of the Grand Rapids Boy Scout camp. Pin is the townsite, not a spot.
new.t: Single 1921 magazine telling; no period record yet. Shifting dune sand. Township park and private dune lots: permission; the power-plant land is excluded.
src: Meima, 'A Forgotten City', Michigan History 5 (1921), pp. 408-9
pinev: GNIS Port Sheldon, on land S of Pigeon Lake (2016 Michigan 1 m lidar). On the lidar the power plant and its round pond lie N of the lake, so the 400 m ring stays on the S (townsite) side; no street grid or maple avenue shows.
new.tovw: Lead grade D (treasure thread): one 1921 magazine telling
